LanguageData.IMP_NoSelection: Select a colonist to see remaining implants.
LanguageData.IMP_WelcomeBody: Implanner plans colonist implants and optionally automates the work needed to produce and install them.
LanguageData.IMP_WelcomeFind: Open Implanner with this button in the toolbar at the bottom right of the screen, next to the view toggles.
LanguageData.IMP_NoPlans: Create a plan to define an implant goal set.
LanguageData.IMP_DeletePlanConfirm: Delete plan "{0}"? Colonists assigned to it will lose their assignment, and plans extending it will stop inheriting.
LanguageData.IMP_RankTiersHelp: Implants can be grouped into 5 different tiers. Placement affects production ordering and surgery (depending on automation options).\n\nDrag to re-arrange items.
LanguageData.IMP_IterTier: One implant tier at a time
LanguageData.IMP_OptManualFloor: Required medical skill for surgery bills
LanguageData.IMP_OptAutoFloor: Assign surgery bills to best available doctor
LanguageData.IMP_OptAutoProduction: Automatically add crafting bills for missing implants
LanguageData.IMP_OptIdleBenches: Only allow bill creation at idle benches
LanguageData.IMP_OptProductionSkill: Required crafting skill for production bills
LanguageData.IMP_OptIntermediaries: Allow production bills for missing intermediaries
LanguageData.IMP_CleanupBody: Implanner created these bills. OK turns automation off and removes the checked bills. Unchecked bills stay in place and are picked up again when automation is switched back on. Reserved implant items are released either way. Cancel keeps automation on.
LanguageData.IMP_AutomationOffBody: {0} spreads this colony across several levels. Implanner cannot carry an implant or an operation across a level boundary, so it stops reserving items and scheduling surgeries rather than deliver half of every plan.\n\nEverything else still works. Keep building plans, assign them, and rank your implants. Add operations yourself and Implanner will track what is installed and what is still missing.
LanguageData.IMP_OptEnableTip: The master switch for everything Implanner does on its own: reserving implant items, scheduling operations, and creating crafting bills. Switched off, Implanner still tracks plans and progress; it just stops acting on them. Switching it off also asks which of its existing bills to keep.
LanguageData.IMP_OptIterationTip:
The order automation works through missing implants.

One implant tier at a time: everyone receives the highest-tier implants first, then work moves down the tier list.

One colonist at a time: finish one colonist's whole plan before starting the next. Colonist priority on the Overview tab decides who goes first.
LanguageData.IMP_OptAutoFloorTip: Surgery bills are restricted to your best available doctor, so a novice medic never fumbles a bionic installation just because they reached the operating table first. The restriction follows the best doctor at each colony as people come and go.\n\nTurn this off to set a fixed minimum skill yourself.
LanguageData.IMP_OptSurgeryConcurrencyTip: How many colonists per colony may have surgeries planned at the same time. Higher values queue more colonists in parallel; lower values keep the hospital and your doctors free. Starts at one per ten colonists.
LanguageData.IMP_OptCountHospitalizedTip: Pawns lying in medical beds or downed and awaiting treatment also take up surgery slots. New Implanner surgeries wait until the hospital has room under the limit above. Switch it off to schedule implant surgeries regardless of who is already being treated.
LanguageData.IMP_OptManualFloorTip: The minimum Medicine skill a doctor needs to perform Implanner surgeries. Bills wait until a doctor at or above this level is available. The value starts from your current best doctor when automatic assignment is switched off.
LanguageData.IMP_OptImplantReservesTip: Implants held back for manual use. Automation only reserves stock beyond these counts, so you always keep this many of each listed implant free for emergency surgery or trade. Production does not count held-back items as available, and keeps crafting until automation can proceed without them.
LanguageData.IMP_AddImplantReserveTip: Pick an implant to hold back from automation.
LanguageData.IMP_OptAutoProductionTip: Missing implants get crafting bills automatically. Implanner counts what plans still need at each colony, subtracts stock and bills already queued, and places bills at capable benches. Bills it created are removed again when the need disappears.
LanguageData.IMP_OptConcurrencyTip: How many benches per colony may hold Implanner crafting bills at once, one bill per bench. More benches craft implants in parallel, but your crafters spend more of their time on implants and less on everything else.
LanguageData.IMP_OptIdleBenchesTip: Only benches with no work waiting receive new Implanner bills. Your own production queues keep priority and implant crafting fills the gaps. Turn this off to let implant bills queue up behind your own.
LanguageData.IMP_OptProductionSkillTip: The minimum Crafting skill for Implanner production bills. Higher values keep expensive components away from low-skill crafters; lower values let more colonists help. Bills wait until a qualifying crafter picks them up.
LanguageData.IMP_OptIntermediariesTip: When an implant bill cannot be paid because an ingredient such as components is missing, Implanner may queue a bill for that ingredient too, if it is a craftable manufactured item. Shortfalls are followed down the whole production chain. Raw resources such as steel are never crafted; you still have to gather them yourself.
LanguageData.IMP_OptReservesTip: Resource floors for automatic crafting. A bill is only created when the colony would still have at least this much of every ingredient left after paying the bill's full cost. Raise a number to protect a stockpile; set it to zero to let production spend freely.
LanguageData.IMP_ImportAddNote: Imported plans are added next to your existing plans; nothing is replaced. A name that is already taken gets a number.
